Rashi on Gittin 66a:10:1.hebrew: צרה היא - שמתכוונת היא לקלקלה, שתנשא בגט זה ותאסר על בעלה:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:10:1.english: She is a rival wife - [meaning] that she intends to ruin her, so that she will marry [another man] with this bill of divorce and become forbidden to her husband:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:10:2.hebrew: בשעת הסכנה - כגון זה שמסוכן למות, ואם לא עכשיו אימתי:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:10:2.english: During a time of danger - Such as this [man], who is in danger of dying, and if not now, when?

Rashi on Gittin 66a:10:3.english: [Even though] they do not recognize - whether this is [the man] who specified his name:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:11:1.english: He sought to mock her - since he did not say, "Give [it to her]":

Rashi on Gittin 66a:12:1.hebrew: אם מעצמו נפל הרי זה גט - דדעתו מתחילה היתה לכך, וסופו הוכיח, והוה ליה כמפרש ומסוכן:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:12:1.english: If he fell by himself, this is a [valid] bill of divorce - For his intention from the outset was for this, and his end proved [it], so he is [treated] like one setting sail or one who is dangerously ill:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:13:1.hebrew: מעשה לסתור - רישא תנא "לא אמר כלום", ואח"כ נתן חילוק בין מעצמו נפל ובין דחתו הרוח:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:13:1.english: An incident to contradict?! - [In] the first clause, [the Tanna] taught, "He has said nothing," and afterwards [he] made a distinction between [whether] he fell on his own and [whether] the wind pushed him:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:16:1.hebrew: מי משוי איניש ברא שליח במקום אבא - דלא מקפיד בהי מינייהו, ומעיקרא להאי ברא נמי שווייה שליח; ועכשיו שמת האב, יתנו לה הבן הזה וחבירו, שהרי הלך הבעל למדינת הים:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:16:1.english: Does a person designate a son [as] an agent in the presence of [his] father? - [The reason he may do so is] that [the husband] is not particular about which of them [serves], and from the outset he designated this son as an agent as well; and now that the father has died, this son and his colleague [the other man] may give [the bill of divorce] to her, for the husband has gone overseas:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:17:1.hebrew: אמר לשנים תנו גט לאשתי - אע"ג דלא אמר "כתבו ותנו", הרי אלו יחתמו בעצמן ולא יאמרו לעדים אחרים לחתום, דלאו בית דין מנינהו לצוות על אחרים, אלא עדים שווינהו. ובגמרא מפרש על כתב הגט, אם יכולין לצוות לסופר אחר לכתוב, או הם עצמם צריכין לכותבו:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:17:1.english: [If a man] said to two [people]: "Give a bill of divorce to my wife" - Even though he did not say, "Write [it] and give [it]," these [two] must sign [it] themselves and may not tell other witnesses to sign, because he did not appoint them [as] a court to instruct others, rather he designated them [as] witnesses. And in the Gemara, it explains regarding the writing of the bill of divorce whether they may instruct another scribe to write [it], or [whether] they themselves must write it:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:1:1.hebrew: דרא רבי אבינא לסילתיה - יטעון רבי אבינא סלו על כתיפו למזונותיו להוצאת הדרך, וילך לו אצל רב הונא רבו, כי על פיו ושמועותיו יזכה במתנה בלא קנין:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:1:1.english: Rabbi Avina lifted his basket - [That is,] Rabbi Avina should load his basket onto his shoulder for his provisions, for travel expenses, and go to Rav Huna his teacher, for through his word and his teachings he will acquire the gift without [a formal] act of acquisition:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:1:2.hebrew: דאמר ר"ה - בפרק מי שאחזו (לקמן גיטין דף עב:):
Rashi on Gittin 66a:1:2.english: As Rav Huna said - in the chapter [entitled] Mi She'achazo (below, Gittin 72b):

Rashi on Gittin 66a:1:3.english: His bill of divorce - [That] of a person on his deathbed:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:1:4.hebrew: כמתנתו כו' - ומינה ילפינן אנן נמי, דמה גיטו, אע"ג דלא פריש "תנו", נותנין — כדתנן במתניתין ביוצא בקולר ובמסוכן — אף מתנתו כו':
Rashi on Gittin 66a:1:4.english: Like his gift, etc. - And from this [statement] we also learn that just as [with] his bill of divorce, even though he did not specify "give [it]," we give [it] — as we learned in the Mishnah regarding one going out in a neck-chain [to execution] and regarding a dangerously ill person — so too [with] his gift, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:3:1.hebrew: לאחר מיתה מי איכא - לאחר שמת, מי מגרשה? ובשעת מיתה הוזקקה ליבם, ולהא מילתא היכי נדמינהו:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:3:1.english: Is there [a bill of divorce] after death - After he has died, who divorces her? And at the time of death, she became bound to the yavam [for levirate marriage]; so regarding this matter, how could we compare them:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:4:1.hebrew: אלא ר' אבא - לאו הכי אתקיף, אלא הא קשיא ליה אדר' זירא דאמר קנה רבי אבינא להא מתנה דגניבא:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:4:1.english: Rather, Rabbi Abba - he did not object in that manner; rather, this is what was difficult for him regarding Rabbi Zeira, who said [that] Rabbi Avina acquired this gift of Geneiva:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:4:2.hebrew: במקצת - ששייר לעצמו, שלא נתן כל נכסיו, ובעי קנין, דהכי קיי"ל בב"ב בפרק מי שמת (בבא בתרא דף קנא:), דכיון ששייר לגרמיה מידי, אינו כמצוה מחמת מיתה, הואיל וחס על פרנסת עצמו, והרי היא כמתנת בריא:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:4:2.english: Of a portion - [Meaning] that he left [some] over for himself, as he did not give away all of his possessions, and [therefore] it requires an act of acquisition; for so we hold in Bava Batra, in the chapter [entitled] Mi SheMeit (Bava Batra 151b), that since he left over something for himself, he is not like one who gives instructions due to [imminent] death, since he is concerned for his own sustenance, and it is like the gift of a healthy person:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:4:3.english: And we ask - [Is that to say] by inference that Rav Huna holds that it does not require an act of acquisition?

Rashi on Gittin 66a:4:4.english: For he is one who gives instructions due to [imminent] death - because he knew that one who goes out in a neck-chain [to be executed] does not return:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:1.english: This is what is difficult for him - How shall he acquire [it]?

Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:2.english: He did not say "wine" - [meaning,] "Give him wine worth four hundred zuz":

Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:3.hebrew: דמי חמרא לא קאמר - "הבו ליה ארבע מאה זוזי מדמי חמרא", דנימא לזבוני חמרא ומיתב ליה:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:3.english: He did not say: The value of wine - [i.e., he did not say,] "Give him four hundred zuz from the value of the wine," so that we would say [he meant] to sell the wine and give [the proceeds] to him.

Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:4.hebrew: מחמרא קאמר - "זוזי מחמרא" קאמר דניתבו ליה, וכי עושין מעות מיין?:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:4.english: He said, "From wine" - He said that they should give him "zuz [coins] from wine" — [and Rabbi Abba asks:] Do people make coins from wine?

Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:5.hebrew: כדי לייפות את כחו - לכך לא פירש לא זו ולא זו, כדי לייפות את כחו, שיהא לו כל היין שלו אחריות: שאם אמר "תנו לו יין", אם החמיץ מן היין מאה חביות, היו היורשין אומרים לו "שלך החמיץ"; ואי אמר "דמי חמרא", ומכרו ממנו קצת ואבדו המעות, אומרים לו "אבדו מעותיך"; הלכך אמר "מחמרא", דמשמע יין ודמיו, שהכל אחריות לו:
Rashi on Gittin 66a:6:5.english: In order to enhance his ability [to collect] - For this reason he specified neither this nor that, in order to enhance his [Rabbi Avina's] ability [to collect], so that all of his [Geneiva's] wine would serve as security for him: for if he had said, "Give him wine," [then] if a hundred barrels of the wine turned to vinegar, the heirs would say to him, "Yours is what turned to vinegar"; and if he had said, "The monetary value of wine," and they sold some of it and the money was lost, they would say to him, "Your money is what was lost." Therefore he said, "From wine," which implies [both] wine and its monetary value, so that all of it serves as security for him.

Rashi on Gittin 66a:7:1.english: Anyone who hears his voice - and he specified his name and the name of his city:

Rashi on Gittin 66a:9:1.english: [They] appear [in human form] - Sometimes they [demons] make themselves in the likeness of a person:

Tosafot on Gittin 66a:6:1.hebrew: דמי חמרא לא קאמר - וא"ת: כי אמר נמי דמי חמרא, הוי דבר שלא בא לעולם, כדאמרינן בפרק האומר משקלי (ערכין דף כ:) גבי "דמי שור זה עלי עולה", ומוקי לה באומר "לכשיבואו דמיו יקדשו", ופריך: והא אין אדם מקדיש דבר שלא בא לעולם! וי"ל, דהתם משום דאמר "לכשיבואו", אבל אמר "דמי שור זה עלי עולה" — משמע התם דלא חשיב זה דבר שלא בא לעולם, אלא הוי כמו דקל לפירותיו, דבעי למימר יקדש השור לדמיו. וה"נ כי אמר "דמי חמרא", בעי למימר שיהא היין קנוי לו לדמיו. אי נמי, כאן היה דמי יין שכבר נמכר, ויין שלא נמכר; והכי קאמר: דמי חמרא שכבר נמכר לא קאמר, וגם חמרא העומד למכור לא קאמר:
Tosafot on Gittin 66a:6:1.english: He did not say: The monetary value of wine - And if you will say: Even if he had said "the monetary value of wine," it would be something that has not yet come into the world, as we say in the chapter [entitled] HaOmer Mishkali (Arakhin 20b) regarding [one who says,] "The monetary value of this ox is upon me [as] a burnt-offering," and [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to one who says, "When its monetary value comes, it shall be consecrated," and asks: But a person cannot consecrate something that has not yet come into the world! And one can answer that there [it is] because he said "when [its value] comes"; but [if] he [simply] said, "The monetary value of this ox is upon me [as] a burnt-offering," it is implied there that this is not considered something that has not yet come into the world, rather, it is like [selling] a palm tree for its fruit, for he means to say: Let the ox be consecrated for its monetary value. And so too here, if he had said "the monetary value of wine," he would mean to say that the wine should be acquired by him for its monetary value. Alternatively, here there was money from wine that had already been sold, and wine that had not [yet] been sold; and this is what [the Gemara] is saying: "The monetary value of wine" that had already been sold he did not say, and also "wine" that stands to be sold he did not say:

Tosafot on Gittin 66a:6:2.hebrew: כדי ליפות כחו - פירש בקונטרס שיהא כל היין שלו באחריות, שאם אמר "תנו לו יין", אם החמיצה חבית אחת מן היין, היו יורשין אומרים לו: שלך החמיץ. ונראה, שלא רצה לומר שיהא כל ההפסד שלו, דמן הדין אין לו להפסיד אלא לפי החשבון, והשתא דכולו אחריות, אינו מפסיד כלל. וא"ת: ורב הונא מה הוצרך להשמיענו, כיון דאמר "תנו", ואע"ג דלא קנו מיניה? הא פשיטא דמתנת שכיב מרע בכולה, או מצוה מחמת מיתה, דלא בעינן קנין! ואומר ריב"ם, דאיצטריך ליה לאשמועינן דאפי' יוצא בקולר, כמו עובדא דגניבא דמייתי עלה, יש לו דין שכיב מרע, דכל היכא דמועיל "כתבו" כמו "תנו", יש לו דין זה:
Tosafot on Gittin 66a:6:2.english: In order to enhance his ability [to collect] - Rashi explained [that this means] that all the wine should be his with a guarantee [of replacement]; for if he had said, "Give him wine," [then] if one barrel of the wine turned sour, the heirs would say to him, "Yours turned sour." And it appears [to Tosafot] that [Rashi] did not mean to say that all the loss would be his, for by law he would only have to lose proportionally [according to his share], whereas now that all of it is guaranteed, he loses nothing at all. And if you ask: As for Rav Huna, why did he need to teach us [that his statement is valid] since he said "Give," even though they did not perform a kinyan [formal act of acquisition] with him? Is it not obvious that a gift of a dying person of all [his property], or one who gives instructions on account of [impending] death, does not require a kinyan! And the Rivam says that [Rav Huna] needed to teach us that even one going out in chains [to execution], like the incident of Geneiva which [the Gemara] cites on it, has the legal status of a dying person — for wherever "Write" is effective just like "Give," it has this law:

Tosafot on Gittin 66a:7:1.hebrew: כל השומע קולו כו' - אע"פ דאמרינן בפרק אין בין המודר (נדרים דף לו:) גבי מודר הנאה מחבירו, דתורם לו תרומתו לדעתו, ודייק בגמרא: לדעתו דמאן? אי לימא לדעתא דידיה, מאן שווייה שליח? אלא דבעל הכרי, הא קא מהני ליה דעבד שליחותיה! ומוקי לה באומר "כל הרוצה לתרום יבא ויתרום" — לאו משום דכי אמר הכי לאו שליחותיה עביד, דבתרומה בעינן שליחות, אלא לענין מודר הנאה דוקא לא חשיב שליחות שיחשב בכך כמהנה ליה, כיון שלא צוה לו לעצמו. או שמא יש לחלק, דהכא לא קאמר "כל הרוצה לכתוב", אלא "כל השומע", דייחד יחדיה למי ששומע קולו:
Tosafot on Gittin 66a:7:1.english: Anyone who hears his voice, etc. - Although we say in the chapter [entitled] Ein Bein HaMudar (Nedarim 36b), regarding one who is prohibited by vow from deriving benefit from his fellow, that [his fellow] may separate his terumah for him with his knowledge, and the Gemara infers: With whose knowledge? If we say with his own knowledge, who appointed him as an agent? Rather, [with the knowledge] of the owner of the pile — [then] he is benefiting him, since he is performing his agency! And [the Gemara] establishes it as referring to one who says, "Whoever wants to separate terumah, let him come and separate [it]" — [that is] not because when he says so he is not acting as his agent, for in terumah we require agency; rather, specifically with respect to one prohibited by vow from deriving benefit, it is not considered agency such that he would thereby be deemed as conferring benefit upon him, since he did not command him personally. Or perhaps one should distinguish, that here he does not say "Whoever wants to write," but rather "Anyone who hears," for he specifically singled out whoever hears his voice:

Tosafot on Gittin 66a:8:1.hebrew: וליחוש שמא שד הוא - דוקא בבור, או אותו שעומד על ראש ההר וראהו בפרק בתרא דיבמות (דף קכב.), ואסור לאדם שיתן שלום לחבירו בשדה דבמגילה (דף ג.), כעין עובדא דיהושע שראה אותו וחרבו שלופה בידו — כל כי האי גוונא חיישינן שמא שד הוא. אבל בעיר, מותר ליתן שלום לחבירו ומכירו בלילה, או לעדים לומר בלילה "כתבו גט לאשתי", ולא חיישינן. וכן משמע בירושלמי דפירקין, דמייתי עלה: ומשיאין על פי בת קול, ומפרש: והוא דחזו בבואה; ומפרש: הדא דתימא בשדות, אבל בעיר, אע"פ שלא ראה בבואה של אדם. ופריך מההיא ד"היה מושלך בבור" כו', ומשני: מצויין הן בבורות כדרך שמצויין בשדות:
Tosafot on Gittin 66a:8:1.english: And let us be concerned that perhaps it is a demon - [This concern applies] specifically in a pit, or [in the case of] that one who stands on top of a mountain and saw him, in the last chapter of Yevamot (122a), and [the case of] it being forbidden for a person to greet his fellow in the field, in Megillah (3a), similar to the incident of Joshua, who saw him with his sword drawn in his hand — in all such cases we are concerned that perhaps it is a demon. However, in a city, one is permitted to greet his fellow when he recognizes him at night, or [it is permitted] for witnesses [to rely on one] saying at night, "Write a bill of divorce for my wife," and we are not concerned. And so too is implied in the Yerushalmi of our chapter, which cites on it: "And we allow [a woman] to remarry based on a disembodied voice," and explains: "Provided that they saw a shadow"; and it explains: "This applies [only] in fields, but in a city, even though one did not see the shadow of a person, [it is permitted]." And it objects from that [case] of "he was thrown into a pit," etc., and answers: "They [demons] are common in pits just as they are common in fields":
